Ride the Kashmir corridor into Ladakh, exit over Manali

A 16-day Kolkata-to-Kolkata rail and motorcycle loop pairing overnight Indian Railways trunk routes to Jammu Tawi and from Chandigarh with a 2,100 km Himalayan circuit timed for June through September.

Why this direction works

Enter via Jammu and Srinagar, exit via Manali and Chandigarh. Most riders instinctively book the Delhi–Manali highway first, which forces your body from 2,050 m in Manali to 4,290 m at Sarchu and over four 4,800 m+ passes in 48 hours. Starting from Jammu Tawi (327 m) through Srinagar (1,585 m) and Kargil (2,676 m) steps your sleeping altitude up smoothly before you ever reach Leh at 3,500 m, cutting Acute Mountain Sickness risk dramatically (Chandigarh to Ladakh Route Guide).

Using two different railheads—arriving at Jammu Tawi and departing from Chandigarh—eliminates 450 km of repetitive plains riding and saves two full days out of Kolkata. Because the high passes shut under heavy snow from November through April, target June to September, with September offering the clearest skies and dry Himachal approaches (Endeavor Ladakh).

16 days

Total door-to-door

Four days on Indian Railways, eleven riding days across Jammu, Kashmir, Ladakh, and Himachal, plus one mandatory acclimatization day in Leh.

2,100 km

Saddle distance

Covers NH44, Zoji La, Khardung La, Turtuk, the Shyok river track to Pangong Tso, Chang La, Baralacha La, and the Atal Tunnel into Manali.

₹42,000

Estimated solo budget

Using 3AC rail tickets and transporting your own motorcycle as rail luggage/parcel; renting a Himalayan in the north raises the total to ~₹67,500.

Indian Railways trunk connections

Book 3AC or 2AC tickets 60–120 days ahead on IRCTC. If you are transporting your own motorcycle as luggage in the brake van (SLR), choose Himgiri Express outbound and Netaji Express inbound—both run conventional/LHB rakes with reliable parcel van capacity, whereas Humsafar Express is passenger-focused with tighter luggage space.

The 16-day rail and road schedule

Buffer at least one extra day in your overall calendar if travelling in June or July, when snow clearance at Zoji La or monsoon landslides between Mandi and Manali can hold traffic for several hours.

Day Route & Mode Distance Night Alt. Key Passes, Stops & Logistics
Day 0–2 Howrah → Jammu Tawi (Rail) 2,021 km 327 m Board 13041 Himgiri Exp at 23:55 (Night 0). Reach Jammu 13:00 Day 2, collect & refuel bike, overnight in Jammu.
Day 3 Jammu → Srinagar (Moto) 250 km 1,585 m Ride NH44 through Udhampur and the Banihal–Qazigund tunnel into Kashmir Valley; Dal Lake evening rest.
Day 4 Srinagar → Kargil (Moto) 205 km 2,676 m Cross Sonamarg, Zoji La (3,528 m), and Drass War Memorial. Gradual climb keeps AMS symptoms mild.
Day 5 Kargil → Leh (Moto) 215 km 3,500 m Stop at Lamayuru Monastery, Magnetic Hill, and Sangam (Indus–Zanskar confluence) before checking into Leh.
Day 6 Leh Acclimatization (Rest) 20 km 3,500 m Mandatory 48-hour altitude rest (LAHDC Guidelines). Print 6 permit copies, inspect brakes & chain, visit Shanti Stupa.
Day 7 Leh → Nubra Valley (Moto) 125 km 3,144 m Cross Khardung La (5,359 m); submit printed permit at South & North Pullu checkpoints. Stay in Diskit or Hunder.
Day 8 Hunder → Turtuk → Hunder 170 km 3,144 m Day ride along the Shyok River to India’s northernmost Balti village at Turtuk (2,900 m) and return to Hunder dunes.
Day 9 Hunder → Pangong Tso (Moto) 165 km 4,250 m Take the Agham–Shyok river route (check water-crossing status at Diskit). Overnight at Spangmik or Man cottages.
Day 10 Pangong → Leh (Moto) 160 km 3,500 m Sunrise at Pangong, then climb Chang La (5,360 m) and descend via Karu. Top up fuel and jerry cans in Leh.
Day 11 Leh → Sarchu (Moto) 255 km 4,290 m Cross Tanglang La (5,328 m), More Plains, and Gata Loops. Early 06:30 start; push to Jispa if energy allows.
Day 12 Sarchu → Manali (Moto) 220 km 2,050 m Cross Baralacha La (4,890 m), refuel at Tandi (last pump before Leh was Karu), and pass through the Atal Tunnel into Manali.
Day 13 Manali → Chandigarh (Moto) 275 km 321 m Ride via Kullu, Mandi, and Kiratpur expressway. Reach Chandigarh by late afternoon; drain fuel & pack bike at station.
Day 14–16 Chandigarh → Howrah (Rail) 1,712 km 9 m Board 12312 Netaji Express at 01:25 (Night 14/early Day 15). Arrive Howrah Jn at 08:05 on Day 16.

Own bike by rail vs. renting north

Bring your own motorcycle if you already own a 200 cc+ tourer. Because this itinerary enters at Jammu and exits at Chandigarh, renting a bike creates an awkward one-way drop-off surcharge (often ₹5,000–₹12,000) or forces you to ride back to the pickup city. Transporting your own bike as luggage on the same train saves ~₹25,500 overall and guarantees you know your machine’s mechanical condition (Ride & Fire 2026 Rates).

To book your bike on Indian Railways (Indian Railways Luggage Rules): arrive at Howrah or Chandigarh parcel office at least 3 hours early (official minimum is 30 minutes for luggage), drain the petrol tank completely for safety compliance, remove mirrors/saddlebags, and carry your original RC, insurance, PUC, and Aadhaar/driving licence (Carbikemovers Rail Guide).

Permits, fuel stretches, and seasonal windows

High-altitude riding leaves zero margin for missing paperwork or empty fuel tanks. Complete these checks before leaving Kolkata.

LAHDC Permit (₹590 / 7 days)

Domestic Indian riders no longer visit the DC office; pay the Environment Fee (₹400), Wildlife Fee (₹20/day), and optional Red Cross fee (₹50) on the official LAHDC Leh portal (2026 Fee Guide). Print 5–6 physical copies—checkpoints reject phone PDFs.

365 km Fuel Gap

Between Karu (35 km south of Leh) and Tandi (near Keylong), there are no reliable permanent fuel stations. Carry at least 5 litres of spare fuel in a sealed metal or HDPE jerry can if your motorcycle’s tank range is under 380 km.

June–September Window

Both highways are snowbound from November through April (Seasonal Guide). Target mid-June for snow walls, or September for crisp skies, dry Himachal roads, and lighter traffic.

Climb through Kashmir to let your lungs catch up, cross Pangong via Shyok, and drop down the Atal Tunnel to catch the Netaji Express home.

Pre-departure checklist

  • Documents: Original RC, valid insurance, PUC, driving licence, Aadhaar, 6 printed LAHDC permit receipts, and IRCTC rail parcel/luggage receipts.
  • Spares & Tools: Clutch and throttle cables, spark plug, puncture repair kit with portable 12V compressor, chain lube, and bungee cords.
  • Cold-Weather Layers: CE-rated riding jacket with thermal and waterproof liners, waterproof gloves, woollen socks, and a balaclava for sub-zero pass mornings.
  • Health & Comms: Postpaid Airtel or Jio SIM (prepaid SIMs from West Bengal do not work in J&K and Ladakh), ORS packets, and doctor-advised altitude medication.
